question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $Q$ shown above. Find the matrix $R$ such that $A=QR$ is a QR factorization of $A.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $Q$ has orthonormal columns, pre-multiplying both sides of $A=QR$ by ${Q}^{T},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}^{T}\cdot A & ={Q}^{T}\cdot QR \\ {Q}^{T}\,A & =({Q}^{T}\,Q)R \\ {Q}^{T}\,A & ={I}_{2}R \\ R & ={Q}^{T}\,A\end{aligned}
$$

 

Note that ${Q}^{T}Q={I}_{2}$ since the columns of $Q$ are orthonormal.

Now, we calculate the matrix $R:$

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
